bib.title: KILT: a Benchmark for Knowledge Intensive Language Tasks

question: How can knowledge-intensive tasks (fact checking, entity linking, slot filling, open-domain QA, dialogue) be evaluated on one shared Wikipedia snapshot so that retrieval and generation components can be compared across tasks, including whether models can provide provenance?
hypothesis: A shared dense index coupled with a seq2seq model is a strong general baseline for knowledge-intensive tasks.
contributions: a publicly-available benchmark of knowledge-intensive tasks aligned to a single Wikipedia snapshot
an open-source library for knowledge-intensive architectures
provenance for all instances, extended by an annotation campaign, enabling joint assessment of output accuracy and evidence
a comparative performance of various modeling approaches

method.summary: KILT maps 11 datasets across 5 tasks onto one 2019/08/01 Wikipedia snapshot (5.9M articles) with a common JSONL interface and provenance spans. Baselines (task-specific, closed-book seq2seq, BART+DPR, RAG, retrievers) are evaluated on downstream metrics, page-level retrieval, and joint KILT scores that award points only if the gold provenance page is ranked first.
method.task: knowledge-intensive language tasks (fact checking, entity linking, slot filling, open-domain QA, knowledge-grounded dialogue)

datasets.name: KILT total (11 datasets)
datasets.preprocessing: map provenance by highest BLEU on matched page; drop dev/test items with BLEU<0.5 for any provenance span (avg 18% dropped, except entity linking); keep all train

datasets.name: T-REx
datasets.preprocessing: filtered facts with >20 provenances and relations with <1000 facts: 113 relations, 2.3M facts

datasets.name: Natural Questions (NQ)
datasets.split: new held-out NQ portion as test

datasets.name: Wizard of Wikipedia (WoW)
datasets.split: unseen split for dev/test, open-domain (no topic given)

models.name: BART (large)
models.other: no retrieval; finetuned on all KILT tasks with fairseq

models.name: BART + DPR
models.architecture: DPR retrieves top-3 passages prepended to input, BART finetuned

models.name: RAG
models.architecture: DPR retriever + BART generator, query encoder back-propagated

other.retrieval: top-5 passages per generation step, used as provenance

other.multitask: trained on TQA, NQ, HoPo, FEV, zsRE, AY2, T-REx, WoW; 150k samples per task per epoch; single-dataset batches round-robin

models.name: BLINK + flair
models.architecture: BERT bi-encoder + cross-encoder; flair finds mentions

training.objective: seq2seq generation of the output string (BART/T5/BART+DPR); RAG end-to-end with retriever query encoder

other.note: Paper gives no hyperparameters for any baseline finetuning; only Multi-task DPR sampling (150k per task per epoch) and the BERT-base FEVER classifier recipe (supported/refuted + neutral class from negative-sampled passages).

inference.samples: single run per system on test; no seeds reported
inference.retrieval: BART+DPR: top-3 passages prepended; RAG: top-5 passages per step; DPR passages 100 words; FEVER BERT classifier uses first sentence of pages from top-100 DPR passages with majority vote; slot filling uses one random template question per subject-relation

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: strict exact match, no post-processing; for FEVER, entity linking

metrics.name: Exact Match
metrics.definition: lowercase, strip articles/punctuation/whitespace; NQ, TQA, HoPo, T-REx, zsRE

metrics.name: R-precision
metrics.definition: r/R, R pages in provenance set, r relevant among top-R retrieved pages; max over provenance sets; page level; equals Precision@1 when R=1

metrics.name: Recall@k
metrics.definition: w/n, complete provenance sets within top-k over n sets

metrics.name: KILT-AC/EM/RL/F1
metrics.definition: downstream metric awarded only if R-precision is 1 for that datapoint

eval.protocol: test sets via EvalAI leaderboard; single run; no significance tests

limits: Provenance may not be exhaustive: other Wikipedia pages can contain the evidence; annotation campaign only mitigates this (kappa 0.3 NQ, 0.1 ELI5).
Provenance for a prediction could come from a different system and this is hard to detect.
In-KB only: unanswerable instances, FEVER NEI label, left to future work.
Provenance is scored at page level; for most tasks R-precision=1 requires the top page right.
Baselines are single runs; no finetuning hyperparameters, seeds, or compute reported; NQ test is 3-4 points lower than dev.
TriviaQA and ELI5 evidence documents are not guaranteed to contain evidence (TQA est. 79.7%).
Closed-book BART/T5 cannot be given KILT scores (no provenance).
Dated: 2019 Wikipedia snapshot, BART/DPR-era baselines, 2020-era leaderboard.

terms.definition: a set of textual spans in Wikipedia that contain evidence for producing an output given a specific input
